group.label: Cache Key Policy
group.comment: Magento hashes the full-page-cache key from every value in the HTTP context that differs from its default, so each extra value multiplies the number of copies Varnish holds of every page. Run bin/magento commerce:cache-vary:policy before changing anything here: it prints how many copies the current settings permit. A guest sends no key at all, so guests and signed-in shoppers never share an object — that part is Magento's design and is not what this module changes.

field.label: Apply The Policy
field.comment: Off out of the box. Turning it on changes the cache key, so every existing cached page becomes unreachable and is refetched once — plan it like a cache flush, not like a setting. It only takes effect when the full-page cache is Varnish. On the built-in cache — Magento's default — it stays inert, because the built-in cache keys through a different identifier this policy was never measured against. Run bin/magento commerce:cache-vary:policy: it says which cache is in front and whether the policy is actually in force.

field.label: Customer Segments That Change Cached Pages
field.comment: Comma-separated segment ids. Leave this empty unless a segment actually changes cacheable HTML — a dynamic block, a segment-scoped target rule or a catalog price rule. Cart price rules do not count: they run on the cart and checkout, which are never cached. Every segment left off this list stops splitting the cache, and n listed segments permit up to 2^n variants. You do not have to work this out by hand. bin/magento commerce:cache-vary:policy checks every dynamic block, related-product rule and catalog price rule, and fails while a segment that changes a cached page is missing from this list.

field.label: Cache Variants Allowed
field.comment: The report fails above this number. It is a convention rather than a measurement: pick what your Varnish can hold copies of the catalogue for, and treat a breach as a prompt to look rather than as an incident.
